sørgmodig.explanation: "Sørgmodig" means "sorrowful". To say you feel sad yourself, use "trist" (sad) instead: "Jeg er trist i dag" (I am sad today).

søskende.explanation: "Søskende" means "siblings". To talk about one person, use "en bror" (a brother) or "en søster" (a sister): "Jeg har en søster" (I have a sister).

søvn.explanation: "Søvn" means "sleep". To say how much you slept, use "at få" (to get): "Jeg fik lidt søvn i nat" (I got little sleep last night). To say you do not get enough, use "at mangle" (to lack): "Jeg mangler søvn" (I lack sleep).

søvnløshed.explanation: "Søvnløshed" means "insomnia". It is built from "søvn" (sleep) and "-løs" (without), the same "-løs" as in "hjemløs" (homeless).

at tabe.explanation: "At tabe" means "to lose", as in a contest. To say you lose a game, say: "Vi taber kampen" (We lose the match). To say you let something fall, it also means "to drop": "Jeg tabte min telefon" (I dropped my phone). To say you cannot find an item, use "at miste" (to lose something) instead: "Jeg har mistet min nøgle" (I have lost my key).

at tabe sig.explanation: "At tabe sig" means "to lose weight". Literally, it is "to lose oneself". Without "sig" (oneself), "at tabe" means "to drop": "Jeg tabte min telefon" (I dropped my phone).

at tage.explanation: "At tage" means "to take". To say you go by a vehicle, use it with the vehicle: "tage bussen" (take the bus). To say you are going somewhere, it also means "to go": "Jeg tager til København" (I am going to Copenhagen).

at tage af.explanation: "At tage af" means "to take off", as in clothes. To say you remove your jacket, say: "Jeg tager jakken af" (I take my jacket off). To tell a guest to take their coat off, say: "Kom ind og tag af!" (Come in and take your coat off!)

related.en: to put on, to gain weight

at tage af bordet.explanation: "At tage af bordet" means "to clear the table". Literally, it is "to take off the table". To ask someone for help after a meal, say: "Kan du tage af bordet?" (Can you clear the table?)

at tage af sted.explanation: "At tage af sted" means "to set off". To name the place you set off for, add "til" (to): "Vi tager af sted til Aarhus" (We set off for Aarhus).

at tage bad.explanation: "At tage bad" means "to take a shower". To say you soak in the tub, use "at tage et karbad" (to take a bath in the tub): "Jeg tager et karbad om aftenen" (I take a bath in the evening).

at tage bussen.explanation: "At tage bussen" means "to take the bus". For other transport, use "tage" (take) too: "Jeg tager toget til København" (I take the train to Copenhagen).

at tage det roligt.explanation: "At tage det roligt" means "to take it easy". To tell someone to calm down, say it as a command: "Tag det roligt!" (Calm down!)

at tage en beslutning.explanation: "At tage en beslutning" means "to make a decision". Danish uses "tage" (take) here where English uses "make". To say a decision will come soon, say: "Vi tager en beslutning i morgen" (We will make a decision tomorrow).

at tage en uddannelse.explanation: "At tage en uddannelse" means "to get an education". Danish uses "tage" (take) here. To ask what someone is training for, say: "Hvilken uddannelse tager du?" (Which education are you taking?)

at tage et billede.explanation: "At tage et billede" means "to take a picture". To say it another way, use "at tage et foto" (to take a photo). To suggest a picture of the group, say: "Skal vi tage et billede sammen?" (Shall we take a picture together?)

at tage fat.explanation: "At tage fat" means "to get to work / grab hold". To say you grab something physically, add "i" (in): "tage fat i rebet" (grab hold of the rope). To say you start a task, add "på" (on): "tage fat på arbejdet" (get to work on it).

at tage fejl.explanation: "At tage fejl" means "to be wrong", about an opinion or a guess: "Du tager fejl" (You are wrong). To say you made a mistake in a task, use "en fejl" (a mistake): "Jeg lavede en fejl" (I made a mistake).

at tage fri.explanation: "At tage fri" means "to take time off", when you decide it yourself: "Jeg tager fri i morgen" (I am taking tomorrow off). When you are allowed to leave, use "at få fri" (to get off): "Jeg fik fri klokken tre" (I got off at three).

at tage hensyn.explanation: "At tage hensyn" means "to be considerate". It is built from "tage" (take) and "et hensyn" (a consideration). To name the person you consider, add "til" (to): "Du skal tage hensyn til de andre" (You have to be considerate of the others).

at tage hensyn til.explanation: "At tage hensyn til" means "to take into account". To say what you take into account, put it after "til" (to): "Jeg tager hensyn til dit helbred" (I take your health into account).

at tage hjem.explanation: "At tage hjem" means "to go home". Here "tage", which normally means "take", means "go": "Jeg tager hjem klokken fem" (I go home at five o'clock).

at tage imod.explanation: "At tage imod" means "to receive / accept". To say you accept something offered, say: "Hun tog imod hjælpen" (She accepted the help). To say you welcome people who arrive, say: "Vi tager imod gæsterne klokken fem" (We receive the guests at five o'clock).

at tage med.explanation: "At tage med" means "to bring along / come along". To say you bring something, say: "Jeg tager en jakke med" (I bring a jacket along). To ask to join someone, say: "Må jeg tage med?" (May I come along?)

at tage medicin.explanation: "At tage medicin" means "to take medicine". To ask whether someone has done it, say: "Har du taget din medicin?" (Have you taken your medicine?)
